definition: a. 无生命的, 非生物的
[医] 无生命的; 生活力缺失的
EN: Non-living chemical or physical component of the environment affecting living organisms and the functioning of ecosystems.
EN: A flat or very gently sloping area on the floor of a deep ocean basin.
EN: The process of determining a specific date (in years or some other unit of time) for an archaeological, geological or paleontological site or artifact.
n. 意外事件, 机遇, 事故, 次要方面
EN: A sudden discontinuity of ground, such as a fault of great thickness, bed or lentil of unstable ground.
n. 自然增大, 添加, 添加物, 连生
EN: A process by which material is added to a tectonic plate or landmass.
EN: A small, glassy volcanic bomb, sphere, dumbbell, or droplet-shaped stone resulting from very liquid magma.
EN: The groups ultrabasic, basic, intermediate and acid constitute a series with progressively increasing SiO2 content.
EN: A small earthquake that follows a main shock.
a. 成块的, 聚结的
vt. 使成团, 使成块, 使聚结
vi. 成团, 成块, 聚结
EN: An indurated rock built of large angular rock fragments embedded in an ashy matrix and resulting from explosive volcanic activity. Occurs typically in volcanic vents.
n. 合计, 总计, 聚集体
a. 合计的, 聚集的
v. 聚集, 集合, 合计达
EN: A mass consisting of rock or mineral fragments.

EN: The end member of the plagioclase group of minerals, ideally consisting of silicates of sodium and aluminium, but commonly containing small quantities of potash and lime in addition. Compare barbierite.
EN: A highly basic substance that dissolves in water.

EN: A type of rock characterized by a high content of Na2O and K2O relative to the other oxides. They occur throughout the range from ultrabasic to acid, but have their strongest expression in the acid-intermediate part of the range.
移置体; 外来体; 外来岩块

EN: A fossil, sediment, or rock that was formed elsewhere and later transported into the location where it is presently found, usually by low angle thrust faulting. An object of this type is referred to as allochthonous. Contrast autochthon.
EN: A fan-shaped deposit formed where a fast flowing stream flattens, slows, and spreads typically at the exit of a canyon onto a flatter plain.
n. 冲积层, 淤积层
EN: Soil or sediments deposited by a river or other running water.
a. 琥珀色的, 琥珀似的
EN: Fossilized resin or tree sap that is appreciated for its vivid colour, usually reddish-orange to gold or yellow.
EN: An important group of dark-coloured, rock-forming silicate minerals, including hornblende, the commonest.

EN: A crystalline, coarse-grained rock, containing amphibole as an essential constituent, together with feldspar and frequently garnet. Like hornblende schist, amphibolite is formed by regional metamorphism of basic igneous rocks, but is not foliated.

EN: Amygdules or amygdales form when the gas bubbles or vesicles in volcanic lava (or other extrusive igneous rocks) are infilled with a secondary mineral such as calcite, quartz, chlorite or one of the zeolites. Rocks containing amygdules can be described as amygdaloidal.
重熔作用; 深溶作用
EN: Melting of pre-existing rock. Compare metatexis, diatexis, and syntexis.
EN: One of several crystalline forms of aluminium silicate; a characteristic product of the contact metamorphism of argillaceous rocks.
EN: Fine-grained igneous rock of intermediate composition. Up to half of the rock is plagioclase feldspar with the rest being ferromagnesian minerals.
EN: An unconformity in which younger strata overlie an erosion surface of tilted or folded layered rock.
EN: An arched fold in which the layers usually dip away from the fold axis. Contrast syncline.
EN: Having the texture of carbonate sedimentary rocks characterized by individual crystals or clastic grains less than 0.01 mm in diameter.
a. [地]非显晶岩的, 隐晶岩的
EN: Said of the texture of igneous rock in which the crystalline components are not distinguishable by the naked eye. Both microcrystalline and cryptocrystalline textures are included.
EN: A light-coloured rock of granitic texture consisting mainly of alkali feldspar and quartz, with subordinate biotite; muscovite may be present.
EN: A body of saturated rock or sediment through which water can move readily.
EN: Contains aragonite and high-magnesium calcite as the primary inorganic carbonate precipitates.
EN: The oldest eon of the Earth's history.
n. 群岛, 多岛屿的海
EN: A chain or cluster of islands.
a. 含沙的, 沙质的

EN: Sediments consisting essentially of sand grains; that is, of quartz and rock fragments down to 0.005mm in size. Conglomerates, sandstones, grits and siltstones fall into this category. Particle size 2mm to 1/16mm.
EN: 1. A general term for any consolidated sedimentary rock composed of sand-sized fragments.
EN: Pertaining to, having the quality of, or resembling sandstone.
EN: An arenaceous sedimentary rock. Like sandstone in its general character but containing feldspar to at least 10%. Formed by the disintegration of the acid igneous rocks and gneisses.
a. 粘土的, 含粘土的, 粘土似的

EN: Sedimentary rocks of the clay grade, i.e. composed of minute mineral fragments and crystals less than 0.005 mm in diameter, as well as large amounts of colloidal material. Apart from finely divided detrital matter, they consist of the so-called clay minerals, such as montmorillonite, kaolinite, gibbsite and diaspore. Siltstones, mudstones, shales, clays, etc. may all be referred to as argillaceous.
EN: Fragments less than 2 mm (0.079 in) in diameter of pulverized rock, minerals and volcanic glass, created during volcanic eruptions.
EN: A sticky, black and highly viscous liquid or semi-solid that is present in most crude petroleums and in some natural deposits.
EN: A region of the Earth's outer shell beneath the lithosphere. The asthenosphere is of indeterminate thickness and behaves plastically.

EN: A complex aluminous silicate of calcium, iron and magnesium, crystallising in the monoclinic system, and occurring in many igneous rocks, particularly those of basic composition. It is an essential component of basalt, dolerite and gabbro.
EN: A zone surrounding an igneous intrusion in which country rock shows effects of contact metamorphism.

EN: A fossil, sediment, or rock that was formed or produced in the location where it is now found. The term is widely applied to a coal or peat that originated at the place where the plants comprising it grew and decayed and to rocks that have not been displaced by overthrust faulting. An object of this type is referred to as autochthonous. Contrast allochthon.
n. (北美洲西南部的) 山麓冲积平原
EN: A series of coalescing alluvial fans along a mountain front.
EN: A distinctive type of rock often found in primordial sedimentary rocks.
EN: A fine-grained, mafic igneous rock composed predominantly of ferromagnesian minerals and with lesser amounts of calcium-rich plagioclase feldspar.
EN: The thick foundation of ancient, and oldest metamorphic and igneous rock that forms the crust of continents, often in the form of granite.
EN: Igneous rock with low silica content (<54%). The groups ultrabasic, basic, intermediate, and acid constitute a series with progressively increasing SiO2 content.
EN: A landform scooped out by water erosion.

EN: A particular topography covering much of the southwestern United States and northwestern Mexico that is typified by elongate north-south trending arid valleys bounded by mountain ranges which also bound adjacent valleys.
EN: A large discordant pluton with an outcropping area greater than 100 square kilometres (39 sq mi).
n. 基岩, 基本原理, 基础
EN: Native consolidated rock underlying the loose rock or soil surface of the Earth.
n. <美>[地质]斑脱土(火山灰分解成的一种粘土)

EN: Swelling clay minerals of the smectite group with many industrial applications (drilling mud, expansive backfill materials...). The name bentonite is inherited from Fort Benton in Wyoming where large swelling clay deposits exist. See also smectite and montmorillonite.
EN: The erosion of hard ocean substrates by living organisms through various biological mechanisms.
a. 生物所产生的, 生物的生命活动所必需的
EN: Of biological origin – Produced by the present or past activity of living organisms, or by a biological process.
EN: Landform of organic sedimentary rock enclosed or surrounded by rock of different origin.
EN: A branch of stratigraphy which focuses on correlating and assigning relative ages of rock strata by using the fossil assemblages contained within them.
EN: The study of the processes that take place after an organism dies but before its final burial.
EN: A distinctly bedded or broadly lenticular sedimentary rock landform.
a. 生命的, 生物的
[医] 生命的, 生物的, 生物区[系]的
EN: Of biological origin – Produced by the present or past activity of living organisms, or by a biological process.

EN: A form of black mica widely distributed in igneous rocks (particularly in granites) as lustrous black crystals, with a singularly perfect cleavage. In composition it is a complex silicate, chiefly of iron and magnesium, together with potassium and hydroxyl.
EN: The displacement and mixing of sediment particles by benthic fauna (animals) or flora (plants).
EN: A rock that forms by the metamorphism of basalt or rocks of similar composition at high pressures and low temperatures, approximately corresponding to a depth of to and a temperature of to.
<法> n.血肠, 香肠状碎肉
EN: A structure formed by extension, in which a rigid tabular body such as a bed of sandstone is stretched and deformed amidst less competent beds. See also boudinage.
EN: The sequence in which minerals crystallize from a cooling basaltic magma.
a. 有盐味的, 令人不快的
EN: Water with a salinity higher than freshwater but lower than seawater.
EN: A rounded, smooth-surfaced volcanic bomb with a cracked surface resembling a cracked crust of bread, hence the name.
EN: A coarse-grained clastic rock consisting largely of angular fragments of existing rocks.

EN: A failure mode of a rock subjected to high compressive stresses, where the actual compressive stress at the point of failure is less than the ultimate compressive stresses that the material is capable of withstanding. Typically, folding is thought to occur by simple buckling of a planar surface and its confining volume. The volume change is accommodated by layer parallel shortening the volume, which grows in thickness.
[化] 石灰质的; 含钙的
EN: Formed from or containing a high proportion of calcium carbonate in the form of calcite or aragonite, used of a sediment, sedimentary rock, or soil type.

EN: A mineral that is the crystalline form of calcium carbonate (CaCO3), showing trigonal symmetry and a great variety of mineral habits. It is one of the commonest of minerals in association with both igneous and sedimentary rocks.
EN: A body of water in which low-magnesium calcite is the primary inorganic marine calcium carbonate precipitate.
EN: 1. A conglomerate of surficial sand and gravel cemented by calcium carbonate precipitated from solution.
EN: A volcanic feature formed by the collapse of land following a volcanic eruption.
n. 寒武纪, 威尔士人, 寒武系
EN: The earliest geologic period of the Paleozoic Era, lasting from 541.0 ± 1.0 to 485.4 ± 1.9 million years ago and succeeded by the Ordovician.
EN: A type of fossil or preservation.
vt. 使碳酸盐化, 使充满二氧化碳
EN: A salt or ester of carbonic acid.
EN: Surfaces of synsedimentarily-cemented carbonate layers that have been exposed on the seafloor.
n. 投掷, 铸成品, 角色分配
EN: The process which occurs when a liquid fills a cavity and then solidifies. If the cavity originated from the decomposition of dead organisms, casting may result in the formation of fossils.
EN: The most recent of the geological eras, which followed the Mesozoic Era.
EN: A fine-grained, silica-rich, microcrystalline, cryptocrystalline or microfibrous sedimentary rock that sometimes contains small fossils.
n. 亚氯酸盐, 绿泥石
[化] 亚氯酸盐(或酯); 绿泥石

EN: Any of a set of allied non-swelling 2:1 (TOT) clay minerals which may be regarded as hydrated silicates of aluminium, iron, and magnesium. Their non-accessible interlayer is filled by a brucite bridge (Mg(OH)2, or sometimes Fe(OH)2). They crystallise in the monoclinic system and are green in colour. They occur as alteration products of such minerals as biotite and hornblende, and also in schistose rocks.
EN: Mechanically redeposited remains of eroded older rocks; i.e. rocks formed of fragments, or clasts, of pre-existing rocks.
n. 劈开, 裂片, 分裂
EN: The tendency of a rock to break along preferred planes of weakness, caused by the development of a planar fabric as a result of deformation.
EN: An individual plate of calcium carbonate formed by coccolithophores which are arranged around them in a so-called coccosphere.
[计] 压缩, 浓缩, 精简, 简缩

EN: The process by which a newly deposited sediment decreases its porosity and progressively expels its original pore water due to the effects of loading. This forms part of the process of lithification.
EN: The process by which rocks shorten or decrease in volume when exposed to certain forces.
[医] 甲状的, 甲介形的
EN: A type of fracture that results in smoothly curved surface faces.
n. 凝固, 凝固物, 结石
[医] 凝结物, 结石; 粘连; 凝结(作用)
EN: A volume of sedimentary rock in which a mineral cement fills the porosity (i.e. the spaces between the sediment grains). Not to be confused with nodule.
a. 聚成球形的, 砾岩性的
n. 集成物, 混合体, 砾岩
EN: Any type of rock consisting of individual stones that have become cemented together.
EN: Metamorphism due to the local heating of rocks by the intrusion of magma nearby.

EN: The layer of granitic, sedimentary, and metamorphic rocks which form the parts of the Earth's crust that comprise the continents, and the areas of shallow seabed close to their shores (known as continental shelves).
EN: Zone of the ocean floor, separating the thin oceanic crust from thicker continental crust.

EN: Extended perimeter of a continent and its associated coastal plain, which is covered, during interglacial periods (such as the current epoch), by gulfs, and relatively shallow seas known as shelf seas.
EN: The boundary between two tectonic plates that are moving toward each other. Contrast divergent boundary.

EN: A type of resin produced by plant or tree secretions, particularly identified with the forms of aromatic tree resins used by the cultures of pre-Columbian Mesoamerica as a ceremonially burned incense, as well as for a number of other purposes.
EN: A fossilized specimen of human or animal dung.
EN: A silicate of aluminium, iron and magnesium with water, which crystallises in the orthorhombic system and occurs mainly in metamorphic rocks.
n. 核心, 果心, 要点
EN: The innermost layer(s) of a planet, referring especially to the Earth's core.
EN: An ellipsoidal or broadly rectangular joint block of granite formed by subsurface weathering in the same manner as a tor but entirely separated from bedrock.
EN: The rock native to an area, as opposed to rock that formed elsewhere and was later transported to the area.
EN: An old and stable part of the continental crust that has survived the merging and splitting of continents and supercontinents for at least 500 million years.
EN: An inclined sedimentary structure in a horizontal unit of rock. Such tilted structures indicate the type of depositional environment, not post-depositional deformation.
EN: A liquid mixture of naturally occurring hydrocarbons.
n. 外壳, 坚硬外皮, 面包皮
EN: The outermost solid layer of a planet or moon, referring especially to the Earth's crust.
EN: An igneous, volcanic rock with a high iron content. It is an extrusive rock of the same general composition as andesite, but a less calcic feldspar. Synonymous with quartz andesite.
EN: Any distinct isotope produced by the radioactive decay of an atomic nucleus.
n. 三角洲, 希腊字母的第四个字
[医] δ(希腊文的第四个字母), 丁种, 三角, 三角形区
EN: A landform where the mouth of a river flows into an ocean, sea, desert, estuary, lake or another river.
n. 降格, 堕落, 退化
EN: The lowering of a fluvial surface, such as a stream bed or floodplain, through erosional processes.
n. 树枝石, 树枝状石, 枝蔓晶
EN: A crystal that develops with a typical multi-branching tree-like form.
n. 滥伐, 剥夺, 剥蚀, 剥光
[医] 剥露, 剥脱, 磨剥
EN: The lowering of the earth's surface through chemical and physical weathering.
n. 免职, 作证, 沉淀
EN: The geological process by which material is added to a landform or landmass.
EN: A major fault in a mountain belt above which rocks have been intensely folded or faulted.
[地质]成岩作用, 岩化作用 .

EN: The process of chemical, physical, or biological change undergone by a sediment after its initial deposition and during and after its lithification, exclusive of surface alteration (weathering) and metamorphism.
杂岩; 混杂陆源沉积岩

EN: A comprehensive non-generic term for a non-sorted or poorly sorted non-calcareous terrigenous sedimentary rock that contains a wide range of particle sizes such as rock with sand or larger particles in a muddy matrix.

EN: A type of intrusion in which a more mobile and ductilely deformable material is forced into brittle overlying rocks; a dome or anticlinal fold of the overlaying rocks which has been ruptured by the squeezing out of the plastic core material.
EN: A soft, chalk-like sedimentary rock that is easily crumbled into a fine white to off-white powder.
EN: A monoclinic pyroxene, ideally consisting of silicate of calcium and magnesium, but commonly containing a variable content of FeSi2O6 in addition, and then strictly known as ferriferous diopside.
EN: A grey to dark grey intermediate intrusive igneous rock composed principally of plagioclase feldspar (typically andesine), biotite, hornblende, and/or pyroxene.
EN: A geological formation often created by erosion of tilted strata.
n<古>.不一致, 矛盾,[地质]假整合
EN: A surface that represents missing rock strata but beds above and below that surface are parallel to one another.
EN: The boundary separating two tectonic plates that are moving away from each other. Contrast convergent boundary.
EN: A sedimentary carbonate rock and mineral, both composed of crystalline calcium magnesium carbonate CaMg(CO3)2.
n. 粗粒玄武岩, 辉绿岩
EN: 1. A basic igneous rock of medium grain size, occurring as minor intrusions or in the central parts of thick lava flows.
EN: A geological formation consisting of symmetrical anticlines that intersect each other at their respective apices.
EN: A drill specifically designed to remove a cylinder of material, much like a hole saw.
EN: An elongated, whale-shaped hill formed by glacial action.
EN: An ultrabasic plutonic rock in which the mafic material is almost entirely olivine, with accessory chromite almost always present. Feldspar mainly plagioclase. See also peridotite.

EN: A general term for hard crust existing as a layer in or on the surface of the upper horizons of a soil in semi-arid climates. Duricrust is formed by the accumulation of solid minerals deposited by water moving upwards by capillary action and evaporating in the dry season. Compare hardpan.
EN: A generally coarse- to medium-grained pyroxene in which are set red garnets. The colour is pistachio green when fresh, but mottled with red when weathered.
EN: The portion of the Late Pleistocene spanning the period between 120 Ka and 8m before present.
EN: The largest unit of geologic time.
EN: The point on the Earth's surface that is directly above the hypocenter or focus at which an earthquake or underground explosion originates.

EN: Any of a set of altered gabbroic and doleritic rocks in which the original pyroxene has been replaced by fibrous amphibole. The rock may be regarded as a first step in the conversion by dynamothermal metamorphism of a basic igneous rock into a green schist.
EN: The simultaneous rising and falling movements of continents, maintaining isostasy.
n. 新纪元, 时代, 时期
EN: A division of the standard geologic time scale subordinate to periods. An example is the Pleistocene Epoch of the Quaternary Period.
n. 腐蚀, 冲蚀, 侵蚀

EN: The displacement of solids (sediment, soil, rock and other particles) usually by the agents of currents such as wind, water, or ice by downward or down-slope movement in response to gravity or by living organisms (in the case of bioerosion).
n. 古怪的人, 漂泊无定的人
a. 不稳定的, 奇怪的

EN: A piece of rock that deviates from the size and type of rock native to the area in which it rests. Erratics usually occur as stones ranging in size from pebbles to large boulders which were transported by glacial ice, which upon melting left them stranded far from their original source. The name "erratic" is based on the errant location of these boulders.
n. 悬崖, 断崖, 绝壁
EN: A transition zone between different physiogeographic provinces that involves an elevation differential, characterized by a cliff or steep slope.

EN: A long, winding ridge of stratified sand and gravel, examples of which occur in glaciated and formerly glaciated regions of Europe and North America. Eskers are frequently several miles in length and, because of their peculiar uniform shape, somewhat resemble railroad embankments.
EN: A semi-enclosed coastal body of water with one or more rivers or streams flowing into it, and with a free connection to the open sea.
EN: A geosyncline in which volcanism is associated with clastic sedimentation; the volcanic part of an orthosyncline located away from the craton.
EN: Bounded by the crystal faces peculiar to the species, used of minerals. Synonymous with idiomorphic.
EN: Changes of sea level, constant over wide areas, due to alterations in the volume of the oceans resulting from the formation or melting of ice caps.
EN: Any of a diverse set of water-soluble mineral sediments that result from the evaporation of bodies of surface water.
[医] 表皮脱落, 鳞片样脱皮, 表皮剥脱
EN: The stripping of concentric rock slabs from the outer surface of a rock mass.
n. 延长, 扩充, 范围, 扩展名
EN: Strain involving an increase in length. Extension can cause thinning and faulting.
a. 挤出的, 突出的, 喷出的

EN: A mode of igneous volcanic rock formation in which hot magma from inside the Earth flows out (extrudes) onto the surface as lava or explodes violently into the atmosphere to fall back as pyroclastics or tuff.
n. (患某种疾病时特有的)面容, 外观, 表面

EN: The sum of the lithological and faunal characters of a sediment is its facies. Lithological facies involves composition, grain size, texture, colour, as well as such mass characteristics as current bedding, nature of stratification, ripple marks, etc. Similarly, metamorphic facies involves the degree of crystallisation and the mineral assemblage in a group of metamorphic rocks.
n. 铺开, 展开;形成气流
EN: Rock deformation related to shear stress.
n. 过错, 故障, 毛病
vi. 产生断层, 弄错
EN: A discrete planar rock fracture which shows evidence of a displacement (the throw of the fault). A fault is a discrete surface.
EN: The zone where exist different discrete fault planes.
EN: Any of a set of the most common minerals in the Earth's crust. All feldspars contain silicon, aluminium, and oxygen and may contain potassium, calcium and sodium.
(pl. falus) (=fals)费尔斯(一种阿拉伯铜币)
EN: A massive metamorphic rock lacking schistosity or foliation.

EN: Silicate minerals, magmas, and rocks which are enriched in the lighter elements such as silicon, oxygen, aluminium, sodium, and potassium. Light minerals (quartz and feldspar) greater than 60% - acid. [Granite (Rhyolite), Adamellite (Rhyo-dacite), Granodiorite (Dacite)]. The term is a mnemonic adjective for igneous rocks having light-coloured minerals in their mode, from "feldspar" and "silica". Contrast mafic.
铁砾岩; 铁质壳; 铁质砾岩
EN: A conglomerate consisting of surficial sand and gravel cemented into a hard mass by iron oxide derived from oxidation of percolating solution of iron salts. A ferruginous duricrust.
EN: Any iron/magnesium-bearing mineral, such as augite, hornblende, olivine, or biotite.
EN: A method that uses tracks that are visible under the microscope to date minerals.
n. 折层, 折, 羊栏, 折痕, 信徒
vt. 折叠, 包, 合拢, 交迭
vi. 折叠起来, 彻底失败
EN: A stack of originally flat and planar surfaces, such as sedimentary strata, which have become bent or curved as a result of plastic (i.e. permanent) deformation.
EN: The parallel alignment of textural and structural features of a rock.
a. 化石的, 陈腐的, 守旧的
EN: Any mineralized or otherwise preserved remains or traces (such as footprints) of animals, plants, or other once-living organisms.
EN: Bearing or being composed of fossils in rocks or strata.
EN: Any crack or discontinuity. In its geological definition, it is only used when no displacement can be distinguished.
EN: A vent in the Earth's surface from which hot gases and vapors are emitted.

EN: A non-standard but widely used abbreviation for one billion (1,000,000,000) years, using the metric prefix G (for "Giga") to indicate a quantity of one billion. When not otherwise qualified, it usually indicates 1,000,000,000 years Before Present (or 1,000,000,000 years ago).
EN: A dark, coarse-grained, intrusive igneous rock chemically equivalent to basalt.
EN: A rock which is or was once held inside the digestive tract of a living animal.
EN: Of geologic origin – Resulting from naturally occurring geological processes.
EN: A special-purpose map made to show geological features.

EN: A mobile down-warping of the Earth's crust, either elongate or basin-like, measured in scores of kilometres, which is subsiding as sedimentary and volcanic rocks accumulate to thicknesses of thousands of metres.
n. 玻璃, 玻璃杯, 透镜
vt. 装玻璃于, 反射, 反映
EN: Amorphous (non-crystalline) hard and brittle solid such as soda-lime glass.

EN: A green-coloured, hydrated silicate mineral of potassium and iron that forms on submerged banks. Its occurrence in sands and sandstones is considered an indication of accumulation under marine conditions.
EN: A coarse-grained, pale-coloured gneissose rock, containing abundant feldspar with quartz, mica, hornblende, and garnet.
EN: The southern part of the supercontinent of Pangaea which eventually separated to form present-day South America, Africa, India, Australia and Antarctica.
EN: A depressed block of the Earth's crust bordered by parallel faults.

EN: A coarse-grained, often porphyritic, intrusive, felsic, igneous rock containing megascopic quartz, averaging 25%, much feldspar (orthoclase, microcline, sodic plagioclase) and mica or other coloured minerals. Rhyolite is the volcanic equivalent.
a. 似花岗岩的,具花岗岩结构的
EN: Any granite-like rock, including granodiorite, diorite, monzonite, and granite itself, among others.

EN: An arrangement of mineral grains in a rock of metamorphic origin similar to that of a normal granite, but produced by recrystallisation in the solid and not by crystallisation from a molten condition.
EN: An intrusive, felsic, igneous rock similar to granite but containing more plagioclase than potassium feldspar. Dacite is the volcanic equivalent.
EN: Statistical distribution of the size of individual sediment grains, or lithified particles in clastic rocks.

EN: An omnibus term lacking precision and applied indiscriminately to basic and intermediate igneous rocks of Lower Paleozoic age in which much chlorite has been produced at the expense of the original coloured minerals, staining the rocks green.
EN: Freshly eroded, angular grains of quartz and feldspar derived from a granitoid.
n. 习惯, 嗜好, 习性
n. 半衰期, 半排出期
EN: The time it takes for a given amount of a radioactive isotope to be reduced by one-half.
EN: Having the properties of certain rocks of igneous origin which contain some interstitial glass in addition to crystalline minerals. Contrast holocrystalline.
n. 铰链, 关键, 枢纽
vi. 靠铰链移动, 依...而转移
EN: The zone of maximum curvature of a fold.
EN: A line joining the points of maximum curvature along the hinge of a fold.
EN: Having the properties of those igneous rocks in which all of the components are crystalline; glass is absent. Contrast hemicrystalline.

EN: An important rock-forming mineral of complex composition, essentially a silicate of calcium, magnesium and iron, with smaller amounts of potash, soda and hydroxyl. Hornblende crystallises in the monoclinic system and occurs as black crystals or grains in many different types of igneous and metamorphic rocks, including hornblende-granite, syenite, diorite, andesite, hornblende-schist, and amphibole.
EN: A hard, compact, fine-textured contact-altered argillaceous rock that breaks into splintery fragments.
EN: A raised fault block bounded by normal faults.
EN: A natural spring resulting from the emergence of geothermally heated groundwater from beneath the Earth's crust.
EN: Pertaining to the actions or products of heated water.
深海热泉;深海热液喷口
EN: A fissure in a planet's surface from which geothermally heated water emerges.
[医] 多盐的(给以大量食盐的治疗法)
EN: Having a saltiness or dissolved salt content greater than that of seawater.
EN: The study of traces of organismal behavior.
EN: Bounded by the crystal faces peculiar to the species, used of minerals. Synonymous with euhedral.

EN: A type of rock formed by solidification of cooled magma (molten rock), with or without crystallization, either below the surface as intrusive (plutonic) rocks or on the surface as extrusive (volcanic) rocks.
EN: Fine-grained to aphanitic, buff to dark brown compact rock with parallel streaks or lenticles of black glass, produced by violently explosive volcanoes.
EN: An oxide of iron and titanium, crystallising in the trigonal system; a widespread accessory mineral in igneous rocks, especially those of basic composition.

EN: Non-swelling clay mineral with a three layers 2:1 (TOT) structure. Its interlayers contain no water and anhydrous K cations responsible for their total collapse. Water and cations diffusion is not possible in these collapsed interlayers. The name "illite" is inherited from the state of Illinois where natural non-swelling clay deposits exist.
v. (使)坚硬, 变得坚硬( indurate的过去式和过去分词 ); 使起老茧, 使无感觉; 变得根深蒂固
EN: Made hard (by heat or compaction).
a. 层间的,夹层之间的
EN: beds (layers) of rock lying between or alternating with beds of a different kind of rock.
EN: body of igneous rock that has crystallized from molten magma below the surface of the Earth.
EN: A chain of volcanic islands or mountains formed by plate tectonics as an oceanic tectonic plate subducts under another tectonic plate and produces magma.
EN: Two crystals that have similar shapes and sizes, usually through the angles.
EN: different forms of an element each having different atomic mass (mass number).
n. 连接处, 接合, 关节
a. 共同的, 联合的, 连接的, 合办的
vt. 连接, 接合, 使有接头
EN: A discrete discontinuity surface without evidence of displacement. See also diaclase or bedding.
a. 侏罗纪的, 侏罗系的
EN: A major unit of the geologic timescale that extended from about 199.6 ± 0.6 Ma (million years ago) to 145.4 ± 4.0 Ma, between the end of the Triassic and the beginning of the Cretaceous.

EN: A non-standard but widely used abbreviation for one thousand (1,000) years, using the metric prefix K (for "Kilo") to indicate a quantity of one thousand. When not otherwise qualified, it usually indicates 1,000 years Before Present (or 1,000 years ago).

EN: An irregularly shaped hill or mound composed of sand, gravel and till that accumulates in a depression on a retreating glacier and is then deposited on the land surface with further melting of the glacier.

EN: A finely crystalline form of hydrated aluminium silicate occurring as minute monoclinic flaky crystals with a perfect basal cleavage, resulting mainly from the alteration of feldspars under conditions of hydrothermal or pneumatolytic metamorphism.

EN: A distinct type of landscape shaped by the dissolution of a layer or layers of soluble bedrock, usually carbonate rock such as limestone or dolomite. Karst topography is usually characterised by closed depressions or sinkholes, caves and underground drainage.
EN: A fluvioglacial landform occurring as the result of blocks of ice calving from the front of a receding glacier and becoming partially to wholly buried by glacial outwash.
EN: A tight curl, twist, or bend in a rock band. See also folding and buckling.
EN: An asymmetric, linear zone of deformation characterised by a tight curled, twisted, or bended rock band. Kink bands may also occur as conjugated sets.
EN: A silicate of aluminium which crystallises in the triclinic system. It usually occurs as long-bladed crystals, blue in colour, in metamorphic rocks.
n. 空白, 空隙, 阙文

EN: A time-stratigraphic unit representing the gap in the stratigraphic record. Specifically the missing interval at an unconformity, representing the interpreted space-time value of both hiatus (period of non-deposition), and degradation vacuity (period of erosion).

EN: Igneous rocks usually occurring as dykes intimately related to larger intrusive bodies; characterised by abnormally high contents of coloured silicates, such as biotite, hornblende and augite, and a correspondingly small amount of feldspar, some being feldspar-free.
EN: Massive volcanic formation resulting from flood basalt eruptions.
[医] 火山石(一种顺势疗法药)
EN: Molten rock expelled by a volcano during an eruption.
a. 以浅色矿物质为主要成份的
EN: A term used to denote a light colour in igneous rocks, due to a high content of felsic minerals and a correspondingly small amount of dark, heavy silicates.
n. 液化, 溶解, 液化作用
EN: Soil liquefaction describes the behavior of soils that, when loaded, suddenly suffer a transition from a solid state to a liquefied state, or having the consistency of a heavy liquid.
EN: The process by which sediments compact under pressure, expel connate fluids, and gradually become solid rock.
n. 岩性学, 结石学
[化] 岩石学; 岩性; 岩性学
EN: A description of the physical characteristics of a rock unit visible at outcrop, in hand or core samples or with low magnification microscopy, such as colour, texture, grain size, or composition.

EN: The rigid, outermost rocky shell of a terrestrial planet or natural satellite. The Earth's lithosphere is composed of the crust and the portion of the upper mantle that behaves elastically on time scales of up to thousands of years or more.
利索型照相排字机, 煤岩类型
EN: Specific types of rock classified according to the standards of lithology.
EN: A fine, silty, pale yellow or buff-coloured, windblown (eolian) type of unconsolidated deposit.
[计] 存储器地址, 多路存取

EN: A non-standard but widely used abbreviation for one million (1,000,000) years, using the metric prefix M (for "Mega") to indicate a quantity of one million. When not otherwise qualified, it usually indicates 1,000,000 years Before Present (or 1,000,000 years ago).

EN: A silicate mineral or rock that is rich in magnesium and iron. A mnemonic term for the ferromagnesian and other non-felsic minerals actually present in an igneous rock rich in dark (ferromagnesian) minerals (greater than 60% by volume). Basic [alkali gabbro (alkali basalt), syeno-gabbro (trachybasalt), gabbro (basalt and dolerite)].
n. 岩浆, 糊剂, 乳浆剂
EN: Molten rock that sometimes forms beneath the surface of the Earth (or other terrestrial planets) and often collects in a magma chamber.
EN: An oxide of iron which crystallises in the cubic system. It is attracted by a magnet but does not attract iron itself.

EN: An 830 to 980 million-year-old basal group of the Western Cape comprising at least eight distinct formations, including the Tygerberg, Piketberg, Porterville, Berg river, Klipplaat, Moorreesburg, Franschhoek, and Bridgetown formations.
n. 斗篷, 罩子, 披风
EN: The highly viscous layer of molten rock situated directly beneath the Earth's crust and above the outer core.
n. 大理石, 石弹, 雕刻品
a. 大理石的, 冷酷无情的, 有大理石花纹的
EN: A fine to coarse-grained granoblastic calcium carbonate that effervesces in dilute hydrochloric acid. Often banded with various colours and sometimes veined.
EN: A narrow, flat area often seen at the base of a sea cliff caused by the action of the waves.
a. 大而重的, 宽大的, 宏伟的
[医] 大块的, 整块的, 大量的
EN: A description applied to a homogeneous rock which lacks internal structure or layers.
EN: Large-scale breccia formed in the accretionary wedge above a subduction zone.
EN: A term applied to rocks which are abnormally rich in dark and heavy ferro-magnesium minerals.
a. [地](尤指火成岩等)中色的
EN: A term applied to igneous rocks which in respect of their content of dark silicates are intermediate between those of leucocratic and melanocratic type, and contain 30–60% of dark heavy minerals.
EN: The era of geological time including the Triassic, Jurassic, and Cretaceous ages.
n. 变态, 变形, 变质
EN: The solid-state recrystallisation of pre-existing rocks due to changes in heat, pressure, or water-rock interactions, i.e. without melting.
EN: A metamorphosed pelite (fine grain, clayey) rock.
EN: A salt of the non-existing metasilicic acid H2SiO3 based on an analogy with the carbonate system.
带状混合作用; 分异深熔作用
EN: Low-grade anatexis: partial or differential melting of rock components with a low melting point.
n. 微体古生物学( 亦作micropalaeontology)
EN: A branch of paleontology which studies microfossils.
EN: An underwater mountain range typically having a valley known as a rift running along its axis, formed by plate tectonics.
EN: A composite rock composed of igneous or igneous-looking and/or metamorphic materials which are generally distinguishable megascopically.
n. 矿化, 使含矿物
EN: The hydrothermal deposition of economically important metals in the formation of ore bodies or "lodes".
EN: A geosyncline in which volcanism is not associated with sedimentation, or the non-volcanic part of the orthogeosyncline located near the craton.
EN: A partly marine, partly continental or deltaic sedimentary facies consisting of a very thick sequence of soft ungraded cross-bedded fossiliferous conglomerates, sandstones, shales, and marls.
n. 模制, 铸造物, 模制件, 浇铸
EN: The process of manufacturing by shaping pliable raw material using a rigid frame or model called a mold.
n. [矿]蒙脱石, 胶岭石, 高岭石

EN: Swelling clay mineral with a three layer 2:1 (TOT) structure whose interlayers are mainly occupied by hydrated Na and Ca cations and water molecules. The name comes from Montmorillon, France. Montmorillonite and smectite are two interchangeable synonyms, the first being preferentially used in the US while the second one is more frequent in the literature from UK and Europe. See also bentonite.
EN: A fold with a single limb which produces a sudden steepening of the dip; the rocks, however, soon approximate to horizontal on either side of this flexure.
a. [晶体] 单斜的;[晶体] 单斜晶体的
EN: Having three crystal axes of unequal lengths, with one intersection oblique and the other two perpendicular.
EN: A glacially formed accumulation of unconsolidated debris which can occur in currently glaciated and formerly glaciated regions, such as those areas acted upon by a past ice age.
n. 竖框, 直棂, 放射状框
EN: A particular type of reworked boudin. The term is likely derived from an architectural structure with the same name.
EN: The common or white mica; for the most part an orthosilicate of aluminium and potassium that crystallises in the monoclinic system.
n. & adj.[地]晚第三纪(的),上第三系(的)
EN: A geologic period starting 23 million years ago and, depending on definition, either lasting until today or ending 2.6 million years ago with the beginning of the Quaternary.
EN: Having the properties of any chemically and/or organically deposited rock, such as limestones, chalks, and evaporite deposits.
EN: One of the plagioclase feldspars consisting of the albite and anorthite molecules combined in the proportions 9:1 to 7:3. It is found especially in the more acid igneous rocks.

EN: An orthosilicate mineral of iron and magnesium which crystallises in the orthorhombic system and occurs widely in the basic and ultramafic igneous rocks. It includes olivine-gabbro, olivine–dolerite, olivine-basalt, and peridotites, among others.
n. 奥陶纪, 奥陶系

EN: A geologic period and system, the second of six of the Paleozoic Era, spanning the time between 485.4 ± 1.9 to 443.4 ± 1.5 million years ago. It follows the Cambrian and is followed by the Silurian.
EN: The formation and growth of mountains related to tectonic activity.
n. 造山运动, 造山作用

EN: Any set of forces and events leading to a large structural deformation of the Earth's lithosphere due to the engagement of tectonic plates. It is the primary mechanism by which mountains are built on continents.

EN: A silicate of potassium and aluminium which crystallises in the monoclinic system and occurs as an essential constituent in granitic and syenitic rocks and as an accessory in many other rock types.
EN: A geosyncline between continental and oceanic cratons containing both volcanic and non-volcanic belts.
a. [晶]正交(晶)的,斜方晶系的
EN: Having a crystal structure with three perpendicular axes all of different lengths.

EN: An obsolete classification based on the totally deprotonated tetrahedral SiO4−4 anion of the monomeric orthosilicic acid, H4SiO4, or Si(OH)4. Compare with the hypothetical and non-existing planar trigonal metasilicate SiO2−3 anion imagined from the analogy to the carbonate, CO2−3, anion.
EN: A crescent-shaped lake found within a floodplain or fluvial terrace created by the cut-off and abandonment of an active meander within a river or stream channel.
EN: A type of vesicular, basaltic lava often with a ropy surface texture.
EN: An indication of the direction of fluid flow (at the time of deposition) visible in a rock.
EN: An alteration product from the interaction of water with volcanic glass of chemical composition similar to basalt or from the interaction between water and basalt melt.
EN: A weathered layer of bedrock.
EN: An exceptionally coarse-grained igneous rock.
EN: A descriptive name for a clastic rock with a grain size of less than 1/16 mm (originally sand or silt).
EN: An olive green when fresh, medium brown when weathered, saccharoidal intrusive igneous rock composed mainly of olivine, sometimes with pyroxene.
EN: The branch of geology that studies the origin, composition, distribution, and structure of rocks.
EN: A large, conspicuous fragment in sediment or sedimentary rock composed of various sizes of material.
EN: A relatively large crystal in an igneous rock.
千枚糜稜岩; 千糜岩
EN: A rock that macroscopically resembles phyllite but that is formed by mechanical degradation (mylonization) of initially coarser rocks (e.g., graywacke, granite, or gneiss).
EN: A feature that is cut by a fault and moved. Reconstruction of that object can show how much the fault has moved.
n. 柱子, 栋梁, 台柱, 重要的支持者
EN: A vertical, standing, often spire-shaped, natural rock formation.
EN: A black, opaque volcanic glass that may contain irregular, whitish clusters of minerals. Resembles pitch in appearance.
EN: The set of natural processes and phenomena which result in large-scale movements of portions of the Earth's lithosphere, which is fragmented into multiple tectonic plates of various sizes.
n. 更新世, 更新世岩

EN: The geologic epoch which lasted from about 2,588,000 to 11,700 years ago, spanning the world's recent period of repeated glaciations. The Pleistocene is the first epoch of the Quaternary Period and the sixth epoch of the Cenozoic Era.
n. 上新世, 上新世岩

EN: The geologic period that extends from 5.332 million to 2.588 million years Before Present. It is the second-youngest epoch of the Neogene Period in the Cenozoic Era. The Pliocene follows the Miocene and is followed by the Pleistocene.
a. [地]火成论的, 火成岩的
EN: Having crystallised at depth within the Earth's crust, used of a rock. Plutonic rocks are slow-cooling and coarse-grained and have relatively low temperatures of final consolidation.

EN: A ladder or grid pattern that occurs during jointing that resembles plumes, oriented perpendicular to the stress, hence which usually form parallel to the upper and lower surfaces of the constituent rock unit.
EN: The destructive after-action of the concentrated volatile constituents of a magma, effected after the consolidation of the main body of the magma.
EN: Water present in rock and soil pore spaces. Also called interstitial water.
EN: A large mineral crystal in a metamorphic rock which has grown within the finer-grained groundmass.
EN: 1. A rock that is porphyritic, containing large and small crystals.
n. 前寒武纪, 前寒武纪岩

EN: A non-standard geologic time period immediately preceding the Phanerozoic Eon, divided into several eons of the geologic time scale. It spans from the formation of Earth about 4540 Ma (million years ago) to the beginning of the Cambrian Period, about 541.0 ± 1.0 Ma, when macroscopic hard-shelled animals first appeared in abundance.
n. 沉淀物, 凝结物, 结果
vt. 猛抛, 使陷入, 促成, 使沉淀
a. 突然的, 猛地落下的, 轻率的
EN: A rock or mineral precipitated into solid form from an aqueous solution.
EN: Rock deformation mechanism involving minerals dissolution under mechanical stress.
EN: Mineral changes in rocks under increasing pressure and/or temperature conditions.

EN: The source rock from which a metamorphic, or in some rare cases a sedimentary, rock was formed. In most cases the appropriate sedimentary term is "provenance" rather than "protolith", since the material has been transported.
EN: A general term for a sandstone, most often used to describe a metamorphosed rock unit with a dominantly sandstone protolith.
EN: A weaker material (mainly lithic fragments) that becomes crushed and matrix-like in a rock.
EN: A light-coloured, highly vesicular volcanic rock of very low density.
EN: A fast-moving current of hot gas and rock (collectively known as tephra), which normally hugs the ground and travels downhill or spreads laterally under gravity.
EN: A volcanic fragment, such as a volcanic bomb, breadcrust bomb, or achnelith.

EN: Any of a set of mineral species which, although falling into different systems (orthorhombic, monoclinic, and triclinic), are closely related in form and structure. They are metasilicates of calcium, magnesium, and iron with manganese, and less often with sodium, potassium, zirconium, and fluorine.
EN: A coarse-grained, holocrystalline igneous rock consisting mainly of pyroxenes. It may contain biotite, hornblende, or olivine as accessories.
a. 四个一组的, 四元的, 四价的, 季的
[计] 四进制的, 四元的
EN: The most recent of the three periods of the Cenozoic Era in the standard geologic time scale. It follows the Neogene Period, spanning 2.588 ± 0.005 million years ago to the present.

EN: Landform comprising an immense pile of calcareous material previously accumulated on an ancient sea floor. Reef knolls can be divided into bioherms and biostromes. A bioherm is a landform of organic sedimentary rock enclosed or surrounded by rock of different origins. A biostrome is a distinctly bedded or broadly lenticular sedimentary rock landform.
EN: Over wide areas resulting from deep burial with consequent rise in temperature and static pressure, usually with the help of folding movements that accompany the formation of mountain ranges.
EN: A basaltic pumice in which the walls of the vesicles have collapsed, leaving a network of fine, interconnecting glass threads. It is the lightest rock known.

EN: The reconstitution of a rock via revolatisation under decreasing temperatures (and usually pressures), allowing the mineral assemblages formed in prograde metamorphism to revert to those more stable at less extreme conditions.
EN: An aphanitic, buff to greyish flow-banded rock, often containing spherulites or phenocrysts of quartz and feldspar.
EN: An elongated post-glacial rock formation with a smoothed surface on the uphill side and a "plucked" surface on the downhill side.
EN: undulating low hill terrain; cf. "Hügelland"
EN: Having the composition and characteristics of clastic rocks, i.e. coarse-grained sedimentary rocks, conglomerates, and breccias, with a particle size of less than 2 mm.
EN: A generic term for any of a set of sedimentary rocks composed of rounded or angular detrital grains, i.e. granules, pebbles, cobbles, and boulders, which are coarser than sand in size.
EN: Having a texture similar to that of granulated sugar.

EN: A form of potash feldspar identical in composition with orthoclase but physically different, formed under different conditions and occurring in different rock types. It is the high temperature form of orthoclase, into which it inverts at 900 °C (1,650 °F). Occurs in lavas and dyke rocks.
n. 山麓碎石, 岩屑堆
EN: A depression in which sediments substantially accumulate over time.
n. 序列, 续发事件, 顺序, 连续
EN: A sequence of geological events, processes, or rocks arranged in chronological order.
EN: A white potash-mica, similar to muscovite in chemical composition and general character but occurring as a secondary mineral, often as a decomposition product of orthoclase.
EN: A tabular to sheet-like, planar or curviplanar zone composed of rocks that are more highly strained than rocks adjacent to the zone. See also fault.
n. 盾, 防卫物, 保护者, 屏蔽
vt. 保护, 遮蔽, 屏蔽, 庇护, 挡开, 避开
EN: A large area of exposed Precambrian crystalline igneous and high-grade metamorphic rocks that form tectonically stable areas.
EN: A beach which is armoured with pebbles or small- to medium-sized cobbles (as opposed to fine sand), typically ranging from 2 to 200 millimetres (0.1 to 7.9 in) diameter.
硅结砾岩; 硅质壳层
EN: An indurated soil duricrust formed when surface sand and gravel are cemented by dissolved silica.

EN: The property of splitting easily along regular, closely spaced planes of fissility, produced by pressure in fine-grained rocks, with the cleavage planes lying in the directions of maximum elongation of the mass.
EN: A smoothly polished surface caused by frictional movement between rocks along the two sides of a fault. This surface is normally striated in the direction of movement.
n. 暴跌, 垂头弯腰的姿态
vi. 猛然掉落, 陷入, 衰落(经济等)
EN: A form of mass wasting that occurs when a coherent mass of loosely consolidated materials or rock layers moves a short distance down a slope.
EN: Series of global glaciations in the Precambrian, 600 to 700 million years ago, before the hard-shelled animal life explosion.

EN: Swelling clay minerals with a three-layer 2:1 (TOT) structure whose interlayers are mainly occupied by Na or Ca hydrated cations and water molecules (from Ancient Greek σμηκτός (smēktós) 'lubricated'; from σμηκτρίς (smēktrís) 'walker's earth, fuller's earth'; lit. 'rubbing earth; earth that has the property of cleaning'). See also montmorillonite and bentonite. For non-swelling 2:1 clay minerals, see illite and chlorite.
EN: The process describing the behavior of soils that, when loaded, suddenly suffer a transition from a solid state to a liquefied state, or which have the consistency of a heavy liquid.

EN: describes the distribution of grain size of sediments, either in unconsolidated deposits or in sedimentary rocks. Very poorly sorted indicates that the sediment sizes are mixed (large variance); whereas well sorted indicates that the sediment sizes are similar (low variance).
n. [地]洞穴堆积物(如钟乳石)

EN: A geological formation by mineral deposits that accumulate over time in natural caves. Speleothems most commonly form in calcareous caves due to carbonate dissolution reactions. They can take a variety of forms, depending on their depositional history and environment. Their chemical composition, gradual growth, and preservation in caves make them useful paleoclimatic proxies. Includes stalactites and stalagmites.
EN: Ancient deprecated name for a calcium titanium nesosilicate mineral, CaTiSiO5.
EN: A red brown to black, mostly opaque, nesosilicate mineral with a white streak.
EN: A beach ridge usually located further or higher inland caused by wave action from storms.
n. 紧张, 拉紧, 张力, 过劳, 扭伤, 血缘, 种, 族, 气质, 曲调, 旋律, 口吻
vt. 使劳累, 拉紧, 过分使用, 扭伤, 滥用, 曲解, 滤
vi. 尽力, 努力, 紧拉, 弯曲, 被滤出
EN: A change in the volume or shape of a rock mass in response to stress.
EN: An irregular discontinuity or non-structural fracture in limestone and other sedimentary rocks. Stylolites result from compaction and pressure solution during diagenesis.
a. 地表的, 地面的
EN: Of or pertaining to the surface.

EN: A coarse-grained igneous rock of intermediate composition, composed essentially of alkali-feldspar to the extent of at least two thirds of the total, with a variable content of mafic materials, of which common hornblende is characteristic.
EN: A geological fold with strata dipping inwards towards the fold axis. Contrast anticline.
EN: An abrupt change in the orientation of a mountain belt or individual fold/thrust structure
EN: A group of rock formations within the Cape Supergroup sequence of rocks.
EN: Natural glass formed from terrestrial ejecta during a meteorite impact.
EN: Storm deposits found in sedimentary formations where shell debris accumulate under the effect of waves and seawater movement.
n. 固执, 不屈不挠, 顽固, 黏性, 韧性
EN: A mineral's behavior when deformed or broken.

EN: Fragmental material produced by a volcanic eruption regardless of composition, fragment size or emplacement mechanism. Once clasts have fallen to the ground they remain as tephra unless hot enough to fuse together into pyroclastic rock or tuff.
EN: A prehistoric ocean that existed between the continents of Gondwana and Laurasia during the Mesozoic era before the opening of the Indian Ocean.
EN: A type of sedimentary rock derived from glacial till which has been indurated or lithified by subsequent burial into solid rock.
EN: A calcium titanium nesosilicate mineral, CaTiSiO5. See also sphene.
n. 地志, 地形学, 地势, 局部解剖学
[医] 局部解剖, 局部记载
EN: The arrangement of the natural and artificial physical features of an area.
EN: A large, free-standing residual mass (rock outcrop) that rises abruptly from the surrounding smooth and gentle slopes of a rounded hill summit or ridge crest.

EN: A fine-grained igneous rock type of intermediate composition, in most cases with little or no quartz, consisting largely of alkali-feldspars (sanidene or oligooclase) together with a small amount of coloured silicates such as diopside, horneblende, or mica.
EN: A terrestrial sedimentary rock formed by the precipitation of carbonate minerals from solution in ground and surface waters and/or geothermally heated hot springs.
EN: In the triclinic system, the crystal is described by vectors of unequal length, and none of the three vectors are orthogonal to another.
EN: A rock formed of compacted volcanic fragments, some of which can be distinguished by the naked eye. If the fragments are larger than the rock grades into an agglomerate.
EN: A vast, flat, treeless Arctic region of Europe, Asia, and North America in which the subsoil is permanently frozen.
EN: The deposit of a turbidity current.
EN: A current of rapidly moving, sediment-laden water moving down a slope through water, or another fluid. The current moves because it has a higher density than the fluid through which it flows.
EN: A component of the PreCambrian Malmesbury group of South Africa
EN: A shallow-water carbonate facies deposited along the northern margins of the Tethys Ocean during the Barremian and Aptian.

EN: A bubble inclusion within mineral grains (typically monocrystalline quartz), filled with liquid, gas, or both liquid and gas. Vacuoles are randomly distributed in contrast to the oriented bubble trains of Boehm Lamellae.
[地质]纹泥, 每年一度的冲积层
EN: An annual layer of sediment or sedimentary rock.
EN: A hydrous silicate mineral that is classified as a phyllosilicate and that expands greatly when heated. Exfoliation occurs when the mineral is heated sufficiently.
EN: The direction of overturning of asymmetric folds, which matches the direction of thrusting.
EN: A group of macerals that are the most common component of coal.
a. 火山的, 猛烈的

EN: Rocks that have crystallised from magma poured out at the surface or introduced at shallow depth. They have cooled relatively rapidly, the grain size of the crystals is small, some part of the melt may solidify as glass, volatiles are lost and anhydrous minerals with high temperatures of crystallisation are present.
EN: Rounded or spindle-shaped rock of mainly basaltic composition ejected during eruptions.
EN: A small cavity in a rock filled or lined with crystals or minerals that are different from the host rock.
EN: A graph that plots wave amplitudes (recorded by seismic reflection and borehole logging) as a function of time, with the positive peaks shaded in a single dark colour.
